answer: The basalt multiplier is published, charged in atlas, and ivory lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4083 identities would post 1054 proofs and burn roughly 22 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
